replacement_or_dependency: The host and device use the event names and Zod schemas for tab, session and host-service messages. Rust carries these messages but does not replace the application contract.
Rust asks for a journal, blob or sign-in callback over remotebytes.ask. Main runs the registered link callback and sends remotebytes.answer to the same core generation.

Rust dials, authenticates and reconnects each host. Main reopens the client, matches replies and owns each deadline. Keep this split until native callers use the link directly: a core.call reply finishes on a separate task, so a later link-close event could reach main first. Today replies and close events use the same output queue; local close rejects outstanding calls immediately.
proof: RemoteClient.request, #onMessage and close; remote/devices/client.rs::Client; remote/link.rs::Task::{drain,run}; core/src/server.rs::serve (finish then enqueue reply)

replacement_or_dependency: Main answers remote.ask by kind and generation, including sharing policy, device approval and host hello. Missing or failed handlers return a refusal to the Rust caller.
proof: onCoreAsk; route calls remote.answer; SharingCore.open; RemoteHost.answerAsk

replacement_or_dependency: Exercises Rust identity and paired stores through remote.identity and remote.store.*. Legacy TS key helpers supply test input, not the implementation under test.
Two RemoteDevices use the Rust loopback link. The TS client validates the host notice and notifies its listener with the host ID. No Autopilot run starts.
Exercises host and peer renames through RemoteDevices and the Rust link and store. Uses fake tailnet discovery and reopens the device on the same user data.

Exercises RemoteDevices over the Rust loopback link, including offline rank exchange, access refusal, failed rank saves, and restoring the accepted order after a core exit. Tailscale and host services are fixtures.
proof: DevicesRig, stopCore, “shared sidebar device order”; native/ompdesk/crates/core/src/remote/devices/order/tests.rs covers the released wire format, ties, malformed rows and eviction

replacement_or_dependency: Rust owns discovery, trust, listeners, reconnects and visible sidebar ranks. Main supplies preferences and approval, mirrors quotas, creates sidecars, and exchanges opaque rank rows over authenticated links.

OMP_GUI_FANOUT_CPU=<dir> enables main-thread CPU and receiver counts. Replays scripted omp events through SidecarPool, the core web router and LocalHostServices. Computer sinks record outgoing JSON for nonexistent link IDs, not delivered socket bytes.

Rust authenticates the peer and negotiates the application hello before asking main for desktop state. Main must subscribe the live connection before the native link starts; it dispatches calls to local host services and observes close on the same ordered stream (§1.3a,c).

Exercises hosted tabs and core-backed storage with fake sidecars and connections. Real multipart storage cases cover byte order, peer isolation, reconnect, quota, expiry, restart and reattachment; no paired network link.

Rust validates the cwd of fresh opens and explicit-cwd restarts in one fs.directory call. Kept calls and multipart uploads already live in core; a link reconnect retains parts and a core restart discards them. Main still authenticates and routes hosted tabs, quotas and views. Reattach snapshots, plan generations and beforeResponse flush are one ordered stream; the H2 pool feed lacks streaming message_update (§1.3a,c).
proof: LocalHostServices.call, #handKept and #answer; fs/read.rs::directory; remote/{kept_calls,upload_parts}.rs; web/uploads.rs::store; host-services.test.ts

replacement_or_dependency: Exercises the TS HostSessionList and SessionListShare cache, delta application and rereads. The injected host read and broadcast avoid a network connection.
Main keeps one numbered SessionListShare per host, applies sessions.changed deltas to a matching base, and shares a sessions.list read when the base is missing or stale.
Exercises SessionSummaries propagation through LocalHostServices and the Rust loopback link. Compares RemoteDevices' copy to the host across a scripted turn and a mid-turn disconnect.
Exercises TS uploadToHost selection of a single request or ordered parts. A fake HostRequest collects bytes and simulates a host without multipart support. No socket or upload service runs.
The device sends one host.files.upload or splits a large attachment into ordered base64 host.files.uploadPart requests. The Rust link carries the frames; it does not choose or sequence the parts.
Exercises TS routing and charging for a hosted tab or local window view. Injects the pool, target window and command handler rather than starting an Autopilot coordinator.
A paired tab's Autopilot command uses the host's actual window and sidecar. After a start, main looks up the run's session and charges the requesting peer.

The host window holds a SidecarLike view of the peer's existing sidecar. Leaving the view removes listeners instead of killing that sidecar; eligible tool and URI requests go to the window through carryOut.
proof: HostedTabView, HostedTabPort, HostedTabView.carryOut and dispose; LocalHostServices.viewSession

replacement_or_dependency: The running Rust devices instance opens remote-hosts.json, validates host records and atomically writes them. PairedHost describes the mirrored record; the remote.store.* RPCs are test hooks, not the production storage path.
Main calls remote.identity and keeps only the public device ID and key. Rust loads or creates the identity on disk and keeps the private key for handshakes.
Exercises the Rust content-addressed disk cache through ImageBlobCache. Supplies blob bytes via a test fetch and checks hash rejection, shared reads, persistence and eviction.
Rust reads, validates and evicts content-addressed image blobs on disk. Main finds references in messages, fetches missing blobs through the host link on request, and substitutes valid bytes.
Exercises the TS RemoteImageReads memory cache with injected file reads, including conditional requests, concurrent reads and eviction. Does not exercise the Rust blob store.
Main shares concurrent workspace image reads and caches data URLs by host, workspace and path. A matching size and mtime reuses the cached URL. This is separate from the Rust blob store.
Exercises the Rust release policy and debounce through KeepAwakePolicy under the core test clock. The Electron blocker is a spy.
Rust computes whether to hold the blocker and when to release it. Main applies keepAwake.changed to the injected Electron blocker and releases its handle if the core exits.
Typed calls to remote.keptCalls; the Rust queue reads legacy rows, enforces TTL and cap, and commits keep and scoped settlement before acknowledging them. Main holds no journal copy.
OMP_GUI_LINK_CPU=1 profiles main with both link adapters in one process over the Rust loopback transport. The scripted streams measure JavaScript-thread samples, not Rust execution time.
Wraps TS event and read codecs to record inputs, returns and sends as compressed parity fixtures. Only OMPDESK_LINK_EVENTS_CAPTURE=write records and writes files. Does not execute a Rust codec.

Replays captured calls against current TS and the actual Rust event codec in ompdesk-core, comparing JSON and sends. This is parity coverage, not production routing. OMP_GUI_LINK_EVENTS_COST=1 adds a TS sender cost report.

Runs installed omp with a scripted loopback provider, then passes the sidecar stream through the TS encoder and decoder. Checks agent_end references rebuild the original messages. Skips when the binary is absent.
Exercises the TS link event sender, encoders and decoders directly. Checks batching, deltas, references and reconstruction with and without negotiated features. Capture for Rust replay is optional.

§1.3a,c: beforeResponse, generation resets and reattach snapshots are synchronous with the main-owned link stream. The native sidecar feed omits streaming message_update. Move this ordered producer and its sinks together; do not add one IPC call per frame.

The Preview caller reads isOpen and sends or closes in one tick; linkLost must invalidate the socket before the next frame. Move this adapter with the device-side link event receiver and the shell Preview sink (§1.3a,c).
proof: LinkRelaySocket.send, receive and linkLost; RemoteDevices.previewRelay; PreviewRelayTunnels.open

replacement_or_dependency: Constructs already-negotiated capabilities for test connections that have no handshake. Production negotiation runs only in the core.

Compares current RemoteSidecar blob reads and RemoteImageReads with simulated 0.86.1 full reads on the same Rust link. Checks identical pictures and transferred bytes. OMP_GUI_LINK_TRAFFIC only enables printing.
Runs a scripted subagent with the events subscription. Compares current TS progress batching and reconstruction to earlier hello capabilities over the Rust transport. Does not launch an older app.
Exercises TS progress encoding and reconstruction for off and progress subscriptions over the Rust transport. Compares delivery with earlier hello capabilities on the same rig.
proof: delivered, DeviceKind, describe("a device that asks for slim progress")

replacement_or_dependency: Exercises transcript reuse across tab switches, reload and device relaunch over the Rust link and disk cache. Also drives local SidecarManager reads for comparison. Printing and export are optional, not the tests.

Default cases exercise capability negotiation, core frame compression and TS event and read encoding on the loopback rig. OMP_GUI_LINK_TRAFFIC=1 adds timed traffic tables. Older builds are simulated by varying the hello.
OMP_GUI_LINK_TRAFFIC=1 streams four scripted subagents and counts actual compressed and sealed host-link bytes for selected capability sets. No released device binary runs.

Pairs RemoteDevices on Rust loopback sockets. Runs LocalHostServices, SidecarManager, scripted omp and RemoteSidecar. Alters hello capabilities to simulate old builds. Counts pre-compression JSON plus overhead separately from actual core wire traffic.
Compares the current renderer transcript reader with simulated 0.82.1 reads over the same Rust link and scripted host journals. Checks content and bytes. OMP_GUI_LINK_TRAFFIC only enables printing.
Exercises TS PeerQuota against an in-memory store, including daily rollover, weighted reservations and refunds. No Rust store or device link participates.

Main makes the local-day limit decision and reserves or refunds requests synchronously against PeerMirror. Rust persists the peer usage and limits through remote.devices.peerPatch; it does not make the reservation decision.
proof: PeerQuota.reserve, refusal and record; PeerMirror.update; SharingCore.peerPatch; peer-quota.test.ts

replacement_or_dependency: The running Rust devices instance reads and writes remote-peers.json, including trust, limits and usage. PeerInfo describes the peer record in main's snapshot; it does not access the file.

LocalHostServices reads has(), associates the target from the tab's own bridge, and drops all tunnels of a specific connection synchronously. Rust owns their sockets. Move the binding table with the tab/connection owner (§1.3a,c).

Rust validates the peer hello and selects the 18 negotiated flags including compression. The device still constructs its outgoing hello. Main matches request, reply and event envelopes while it owns the per-link request map and synchronous close listeners (§1.3a,c).
Exercises the TS command classifier and compares its tables with the RPC command union. Checks conditional model calls and unknown commands. No commands execute.
The host classifies each tab command before reserving a model request. Conditional commands inspect their payload; unknown commands count against the quota. Rust storage does not classify commands.
proof: commandUsesModel; everyCommandClassified; LocalHostServices uses commandUsesModel; quota-commands.test.ts

replacement_or_dependency: Exercises the TS readoptHostTabs decision to start a deferred tab or open an unheld session, including overlapping asks. Injects kept-tab reads and tab operations instead of contacting a host.

When a host reconnects, main reads tabs.kept, starts the local tab already holding each session or opens the missing tab in a front window. This uses the local pool and window callbacks, not the Rust reconnect loop.
proof: readoptHostTabs; HostTabReadopt.holder, start and open; readopt.test.ts

replacement_or_dependency: Exercises the TS RemoteSidecar and PendingTabCloses with an injected FakeLink, including event decoding, reattach, buffered replies and deferred closes. Blob and sign-in cases use core-backed adapters, not a paired transport.

§1.3a,c: handleEvent reconstructs tab.event and updates the SidecarLike state for the pool in one tick; a decoder-only port sends the full event back over IPC. Move with the ordered device event source. Link loss retains pending replies and closes.
Main still reads host run charges with synchronous readJson. The live Rust peer and host stores replace trust-file I/O only; LocalHostServices saves its own charges through AtomicSaver.

Rust owns devices, stores for paired computers, discovery, gate, listeners and sidebar rank merges. Main mirrors state, answers policy and approval, and reopens devices after a core exit. Sidebar rank writes stay with SafeStore until its whole-file retry and shared pending value move together. Reopen reads that value, not stale disk rows.
Exercises the TS callback parser and the actual Rust loopback HTTP listener via startSignInRelay. Checks forwarding, rejection and shutdown with a test callback instead of a real sign-in.

Rust listens on loopback and validates each sign-in callback's host, path and state. Main supplies the redirect parameters, forwards an accepted callback over the paired link and reports the listener state.
Exercises Rust paired host and peer persistence through RPC. Compares bytes, modes, reload behavior and malformed entries against the old TS format. Does not run the old stores.

Creates RemoteDevices with separate user data, injected preferences and fake Tailscale status and whois. The Rust listener and dialer still connect via real loopback sockets. Tests can replace the default host service stubs.
Retains the released TS frame codec, encryption, deflate and handshakes as an independent test peer. Production uses the Rust link and handshake, never this peer.
Tests the TS fixture's loopback port allocator, including disjoint allocations within a process and separate runner and worker bands. Does not test the product listener.
Probes contiguous loopback ports and separates Vitest and Playwright workers into port bands. Releases the temporary servers before returning a starting port. Not production port selection.
Seeds and inspects the actual Rust paired stores through remote.store.* RPC, reloading on first use. Exposes old store operations for tests but does not implement persistence in TS.
Implements a scripted NDJSON omp peer and optional bridge methods for traffic tests. Emits deterministic stream and subagent scenarios and serves test transcripts and blobs. Not installed stock omp.
Exercises the Rust journal and tail-page disk cache through TranscriptCache with a simulated host fetch. Covers restart, partial writes, concurrent readers, versions and eviction.

Rust stores journal segments and versioned tail pages, serializes reads per key and evicts old data. Main fetches the host's tail at the requested offset and combines the response with the cached messages.

Exercises the Rust host listener, handshake, dial, reconnect and encrypted link via SharingCore, RemoteHost and RemoteClient on real loopback sockets. The tailnet gate is fake. Protocol cases construct legacy peer messages with TS helpers.
proof: SharingCore, RemoteHost, RemoteClient, connectFirst, probeHost, legacyIdentity

replacement_or_dependency: Connects the actual Rust link to the released TS link on a real socket. Checks framing, deflate, encryption, liveness and rejection of malformed input in Rust. Supplies test keys rather than running the handshake.

Rust owns the live socket, frame boundaries, sealing, deflate context and liveness. Main serializes and caps outgoing application JSON, sends it with remote.send, and routes incoming messages by link ID.
